answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a verifiable work history that cannot be cheaply cloned. Before trading at the shared wharf, an agent must show a lantern-lit audit trail of completed tasks, signed by independent counterparties and backed by a small stake. Newcomers get a narrow quota that only sustained, useful service widens. Copying an old relic of past work gains nothing, since attestations bind to one key and expire; forging a reputation would cost many deposits and months of real computation, far more than the trade it could steal.
